sources.title: Climate micro-mobilities as adaptation practice in the Pacific: the case of Samoa
sources.organization: Anita Latai-Niusulu, Masami Tsujita and Andreas Neef; Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
sources.temporal_coverage: Talanoa fieldwork June–August 2021; mobility histories cover participants' prior 10–30 years; site context includes 2016 census data and 2009 tsunami experience.
sources.methodology: Qualitative comparison using Samoan-language talanoa interviews; 40 households invited across two sites.
sources.limitations: Small non-random sample; mixed movement drivers; not prevalence or causal-violence research.

sources.title: The effects of Climate Change on the small village of Salei'a
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate risks and Adaptation Fund-supported works reported as of October 2019; programme began in 2013.
sources.methodology: UNDP project case story drawing on project information and a statement by Salei'a's mayor.
sources.limitations: Sponsored project account, not an independent impact evaluation; reported completion and benefits are bounded to the article's 2019 account.

sources.title: Community-Based Adaptation in Small Island Developing States, and Mekong-Asia-Pacific Regions
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Global Environment Facility Small Grants Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional programme case account, including Matafa'a outcomes reported during and after the 2011 El Niño drought.
sources.methodology: UNDP-GEF SGP regional report summarizing Matafa'a adaptation-project implementation.
sources.limitations: Programme-reported, not independently evaluated; historical, not current water status.

sources.title: Pacific Peoples and Climate-Related (Im)Mobility: A Synthesis Report on Scale, Pattern and Impact, Now and in the Future
sources.organization: Bruce Burson, Evelyn Marsters, Richard Bedford and Sandy Morrison; prepared for New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.temporal_coverage: Synthesis published June 2024, drawing on earlier and commissioned Pacific household, community and mobility research; Samoa examples include 2009 tsunami relocation and 2023–2024 fieldwork synthesis.
sources.methodology: Synthesis of published/commissioned Pacific studies, case reports, fieldwork and policy sources.
sources.limitations: Regional, not Samoa prevalence research; violence signal is caveated.

sources.title: Pacific Region Preparedness, Adaptation, and Resilience Program – Samoa Project: Environmental and Social Management Framework
sources.organization: Government of Samoa, Pacific Region Preparedness, Adaptation and Resilience Program – Samoa Project
sources.temporal_coverage: Framework dated June 2025 for a six-year project planned to begin in August 2025; township-plan works and risks were preliminary at report date.
sources.methodology: Project framework identifying preliminary risks, safeguards and responsibilities.
sources.limitations: Preparation-stage risks and plans, not outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: Rural coastal Salani had 93% of 88 households on customary land; inland suburban Vaitele had 80% of about 1,300 households on freehold land.
claims.limitations: 2016 site census, not current national shares.

claims.locator: Section 6(a), 'Climate responses and other mobility drivers', Salani findings.
claims.paraphrase: At Salani, 10/20 participants partly or fully linked inland moves to climate factors (four entirely); storm surge and cyclone rainfall were recurring triggers.
claims.limitations: Self-reported reasons; climate was difficult to isolate from tsunami and social drivers.

claims.locator: Section 6(a), 'Climate responses and other mobility drivers', Vaitele findings.
claims.paraphrase: At Vaitele, 6/20 households linked movement partly or fully to climate factors; seven participants cited social reasons and seven freehold access, with overlap in environmental changes.
claims.limitations: Self-reported, overlapping reasons; family tensions are not characterized as violence.

claims.locator: Section 6(c), 'Micro-mobility patterns'; Section 7, 'fa'a-'āigalua as climate adaptation strategy'.
claims.paraphrase: Seventeen of 20 Salani households near water moved inland; short moves were easier where customary access avoided land-purchase costs.
claims.limitations: One rural village; clearing land and connecting utilities still cost time and money.

claims.locator: Opening paragraphs and Salei'a mayor's statement, article dated 28 October 2019.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP described Salei'a as exposed to sea-level rise, flooding, erosion, stronger tropical storms, rainfall and heat; by 2019 a revetment and raised bridge provided daily access and a disaster escape route.
claims.limitations: The sponsored project story reports implementation by October 2019; it is not an independent evaluation or current condition survey.

claims.locator: Matafa'a, report PDF p.9, community vulnerability narrative.
claims.paraphrase: At Matafa'a, runoff, land management, variable rain, floods and drought were linked to poor water quality and livelihood and health effects; elderly people, women and children bore water-collection burdens.
claims.limitations: Programme case; no population estimate or separation of climate and land-use effects.

claims.locator: Matafa'a, report PDF p.9, adaptation outcomes narrative.
claims.paraphrase: The report says a mountain gravity-fed system and native reforestation were installed; Matafa'a had water during the three-month September 2011 El Niño drought, with clean water in all homes.
institutions: United Nations Development Programme Global Environment Facility Small Grants Programme
claims.limitations: Programme-attributed historical outcome, not independently evaluated.

claims.locator: Matafa'a, report PDF p.9, community-managed scheme and maintenance account.
claims.paraphrase: Matafa'a's community-managed scheme set a household maintenance fee; the Independent Water Scheme Association supported filter maintenance and water quality.
claims.limitations: Arrangements are reported for the project period, not verified as current.

claims.locator: Chapter 'Women and (Im)Mobility in the Context of Climate Change', 'Economic Impacts and Opportunities', report p.96.
claims.paraphrase: Women at a Lalomanu workshop said inland relocation reduced sea access and coastal-road customers for craft and seafood businesses.
claims.limitations: Workshop account; cited passage does not identify the relocation trigger or effect size.

claims.locator: Table 5, Samoa–Tonga fieldwork findings, 'Impacts' row, printed p.149.
claims.paraphrase: The Samoa–Tonga fieldwork summary notes increased domestic violence in Samoa but warns that sampling or cultural factors may explain the difference; it was not raised in Tonga.
claims.limitations: No denominator or prevalence estimate; the report does not establish climate mobility as the cause.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The mobility-impacts comparison flags a domestic-violence signal but cautions that sampling or culture may explain it.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed pp.1–2; Project Description, printed pp.6–7.
claims.paraphrase: In June 2025, PREPARE planned six years of hazard monitoring, early warning, response and urban resilience work, with township planning focused on Sālelologa.
institutions: Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure
Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
claims.limitations: June 2025 project design; delivery not confirmed.

claims.locator: Section 5.3.2, preliminary Sālelologa social risks, printed p.40; risk analysis table, printed p.53.
claims.paraphrase: The ESMF identifies Sālelologa land disputes as a potential planning conflict risk; proposed controls map disputes, exclude disputed areas and use consultation and grievance handling.
institutions: Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure
claims.limitations: Prospective project risk, not observed or climate-caused conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Ongoing land disputes may cause social tensions, conflict and civil unrest during planning.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Section 5.3.2 and preliminary risk analysis table, printed pp.40 and 53.

claims.locator: Section 5.3.2, preliminary Sālelologa social risks, printed p.40.
claims.paraphrase: The ESMF flags possible exclusion of women, youth, people with disabilities and other marginalized groups from Sālelologa planning.
claims.limitations: Anticipated risk, not evidence exclusion occurred.

search_audit.query: Samoa named village climate vulnerability flooding coastal erosion water security community adaptation Salani Vaitele Matafa'a Salei'a
search_audit.outcome: Directly read a 2021 two-village study and local project accounts for Salei'a and Matafa'a; older community assessment surfaced but not added to avoid duplicating the local evidence set.

search_audit.query: Samoa climate mobility conflict violence land disputes family tension domestic violence climate change fieldwork
search_audit.outcome: The regional synthesis reports a caveated Samoa domestic-violence signal in its mobility impacts comparison; the local Vaitele study reports family tensions as a separate movement factor. No causal climate-to-violence finding was established.

search_audit.query: Samoa land dispute conflict civil unrest climate adaptation township resilience project constraints reverse climate FCV
search_audit.outcome: The 2025 PREPARE ESMF identifies existing Sālelologa land disputes as a potential source of conflict risk for project planning and calls for mapping, exclusion of disputed areas, consultation and grievance handling; this is prospective, not observed climate-caused conflict.

search_audit.query: Samoa local climate resilience customary land mobility community water management coastal adaptation project Salei'a Matafa'a
search_audit.outcome: The directly read sources document customary-land micro-mobility in Salani, completed coastal access works at Salei'a, Matafa'a's community-managed drought-resilient water system, and planned Sālelologa resilience and safeguard systems.

gaps: No directly read Samoa source established that climate change caused violent conflict; the domestic-violence signal in the Pacific synthesis is explicitly caveated and non-causal.

The 2025 PREPARE land-dispute and inclusion statements are preliminary planning risks, not realized project impacts; project status should be refreshed before treating planned safeguards as implemented.
UNDP and GEF SGP community results are programme-reported rather than independently evaluated; Matafa'a water findings refer to the 2011 drought and project-era conditions.
The 2017 Samoa Ombudsman climate-rights report was excluded from findings because its reuse notice requires permission for external/public use.
